query: What should I focus on in this table to identify actions that could improve product scores?

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Review sentiment is largely an expression/consequence of the reviewer's score experience, sitting on the path between the review content and the numeric score rather than being a common cause; treating it as a driver of score risks reverse-causation/mediation.

per_column.name: product_avg_score
per_column.rationale: Product-level baseline quality plausibly causes both which review attributes are present (treatment) and the individual score (outcome), acting as a common cause; not named in the query.

per_column.name: score_vs_product_avg
per_column.rationale: This is a re-centered version of the score itself (Score minus product_avg_score); it is essentially the outcome, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Helpfulness votes are caused by both review content and score/perception; it is a downstream effect (collider), and conditioning on it would induce bias rather than remove it.

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: Engagement/effort proxy that could jointly influence both the review's expressed attributes (treatment) and the score given (outcome); weakly plausible common cause, not named in query.

per_column.name: flag_quality
per_column.rationale: A candidate actionable cause: whether the review raises product-quality issues, whose effect on score is the attribution target ('actions that could improve product scores').

per_column.name: flag_taste
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause capturing taste-related mentions; an actionable attribute whose effect on score can be estimated.

per_column.name: flag_misleading
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: mentions of misleading description, an actionable driver of score.

per_column.name: flag_shipping
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: shipping-related complaints, an actionable driver of score.

per_column.name: flag_value
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause: value/price mentions, an actionable driver of score.

judge.rationale: The system supplies a clear TREATMENT set: multiple thematic flags (quality, taste, misleading, shipping, value) that operationalise actionable candidate causes of the product score, satisfying requirement (a). Requirement (b) is only weakly met. product_avg_score is a genuine, query-surfaced common cause of both which review themes appear and the individual score, giving some real confounder evidence. review_length is a weaker candidate common cause. However, several added columns are NOT valid confounders: sentiment is a mediator/reverse-caused expression of the score, score_vs_product_avg is essentially the outcome itself, and helpfulness_ratio is a downstream collider whose adjustment would bias the estimate. So the causal setup has treatments plus one solid non-query confounder, but is diluted by mediators/colliders mislabelable as adjustments, yielding modest confounder quality.
